entry.title: Re: Custom UIBBs not updating data after 2025 upgrade in...
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Here is the response our internal chatbot provided. Please check whether it helps you resolve the error.

Kind regards,

Henrike

#AI-Generated Content

MDG BP Governance — Custom UIBB Not Refreshing After 2025 Upgrade

Root Cause Analysis

The silent failure (no errors, but UIBB empty) after an upgrade almost always falls into one of these categories. They should be investigated in this order:

Cause 1 — UIBB Reads from Persistence, Not the Delta Buffer (Most Common)

Before the 2025 upgrade, the FPM page lifecycle may have triggered a full round-trip that accidentally caused the UIBB to re-read. Post-upgrade, the lifecycle is tighter and the UIBB must explicitly read from the delta buffer.
In your custom UIBB's GET_DATA / DO_INIT / PROCESS_EVENT:
METHOD get_uibb_data.
 
DATA: lo_delta_read TYPE REF TO if_usmd_delta_buffer_read,
lt_zleg_po TYPE TABLE OF your_zleg_po_structure,
lv_found TYPE abap_bool.
 
" *** ALWAYS read from the DELTA BUFFER, not SELECT from DB ***
lo_delta_read = mo_gov_api->get_buffer( )->get_read_access( ).
 
lo_delta_read->read_data(
EXPORTING
iv_entity_type_name = 'ZLEG_PO' " Your custom entity type
is_selection = VALUE #(
( fieldname = 'KEY_FIELD'
option = 'EQ'
sign = 'I'
low = ms_key-key_field ) )
IMPORTING
et_data = lt_zleg_po
ev_data_found = lv_found
).
 
IF lv_found = abap_false.
" Buffer entry does not exist yet — handle gracefully
RETURN.
ENDIF.
 
" Bind to your UIBB context node
mo_context_node->set_attribute(
EXPORTING
iv_attr_name = 'TABLE'
iv_value = lt_zleg_po ).
 
ENDMETHOD.

Cause 2 — Cross-Entity BAdI Writes with Wrong Change Mode

In MDG 2025, write_data without an explicit iv_change_mode defaults differently than in prior releases. You must pass the correct mode, especially for insert/update on Type 4 custom entities.
Corrected cross-entity BAdI derivation:
METHOD if_usmd_rule_service~derive.
 
DATA: lo_buffer_write TYPE REF TO if_usmd_delta_buffer_write,
ls_zleg_po TYPE your_zleg_po_structure,
lt_zleg_po TYPE TABLE OF your_zleg_po_structure.
 
" --- Derive your custom entity from the standard PO/SO ---
" (your existing derivation logic here)
MOVE-CORRESPONDING is_purchase_org TO ls_zleg_po.
ls_zleg_po-custom_field_1 = ... " legacy mapping
APPEND ls_zleg_po TO lt_zleg_po.
 
" --- Write to delta buffer ---
lo_buffer_write = io_services->get_buffer( )->get_write_access( ).
 
lo_buffer_write->write_data(
EXPORTING
iv_entity_type_name = 'ZLEG_PO'
" *** CRITICAL: explicit change mode required in 2025 ***
iv_change_mode = if_usmd_delta_buffer_write=>co_change_mode_insert_update
it_data = lt_zleg_po
).
 
" --- IMPORTANT: Invalidate any cached read for this entity ---
" This forces the UIBB to re-fetch on next render
io_services->get_buffer( )->invalidate_read_cache(
iv_entity_type_name = 'ZLEG_PO' ).
 
ENDMETHOD.
Note: The constant name for change mode varies slightly by MDG release — check your system for co_change_mode_insert_update vs gc_change_mode_update in IF_USMD_DELTA_BUFFER_WRITE.

Cause 3 — UIBB Not Flagged for Refresh After BAdI Execution

In FPM / MDG 2025, the NEEDS_REFRESH method is evaluated more strictly. Your UIBB must signal it needs to re-render whenever the underlying buffer changes.
In your UIBB class, override NEEDS_REFRESH:
METHOD if_fpm_ui_building_block~needs_refresh.
 
" Option A: Always refresh (safe but slightly less performant)
rv_needs_refresh = abap_true.
 
" --- OR ---
 
" Option B: Check if the custom entity buffer was touched (preferred)
DATA: lo_delta_read TYPE REF TO if_usmd_delta_buffer_read.
lo_delta_read = mo_gov_api->get_buffer( )->get_read_access( ).
 
lo_delta_read->has_pending_changes(
EXPORTING
iv_entity_type_name = 'ZLEG_PO'
IMPORTING
ev_has_changes = rv_needs_refresh
).
 
ENDMETHOD.

Cause 4 — FPM Event Not Raised to Trigger UIBB Re-render

If the BAdI derivation runs on a button press or value-help select, you must explicitly raise an FPM event to cause UIBBs to re-render. This used to happen implicitly in older MDG versions.
Raise FPM event after the derivation (e.g., in the BP Governance Controller):
DATA: lo_fpm TYPE REF TO if_fpm,
lo_event TYPE REF TO cl_fpm_event.
 
lo_fpm = cl_fpm_factory=>get_instance( ).
 
" Raise standard MDG refresh event
lo_event = cl_fpm_event=>create_by_id(
iv_event_id = if_usmd_gov_api=>gc_event_data_changed ).
 
lo_fpm->raise_event( io_event = lo_event ).

Cause 5 — Custom Type 4 Entity Not Registered with the UI Refresh Framework (2025-Specific)

In MDG 2025, there is an internal registry that tracks which entity types participate in the reactive UI refresh. Standard entities are pre-registered; custom Type 4 entities must be registered via customizing or the BAdI USMD_GOV_API_USMD_CUST_ETYPES.
Check in transaction MDGIMG:
Master Data Governance → General Settings → Data Modeling → Edit Entity Types and Storage Attributes → verify your ZLEG_PO and ZLEG_SO have UI Integration = Active in the 2025 customizing table.

Recommended Fix Sequence

 
Step Action
1Set breakpoint in write_data — confirm it is reached and lt_data is non-empty
2Immediately after write_data, call read_data for the same entity — confirm buffer holds the data
3Set breakpoint in UIBB's data-reading method — check whether it reads from DB or buffer
4Add NEEDS_REFRESH = abap_true and re-test
5Add iv_change_mode explicitly to write_data and re-test
6Verify ZLEG_PO / ZLEG_SO entity type UI registration in MDGIMG
The most frequently seen fix post-2025 upgrade is the combination of Cause 1 + Cause 3: the UIBB was accidentally reading from the database instead of the buffer, and NEEDS_REFRESH was returning abap_false so even the buffer read was being skipped entirely.

SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud Maintenance Calendar – Downtime Identification

The SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition maintenance calendar uses color coding and box types to distinguish between different maintenance activities. Each type carries a defined downtime window, and the calendar explicitly communicates whether a given weekend involves disruptive or potentially non-disruptive activity. [1] [2] [3]

Non-Disruptive vs. Disruptive Maintenance
Maintenance Type Calendar Indicator Downtime Required API Suspension Recommended
Global Infrastructure MaintenanceDark blue cell backgroundYes – uses full downtime windowYes
Standard Maintenance Weekend (from Sep 2026)Dark green cell backgroundYes – planned downtime for P, T, D systems once/monthYes
Online Software Change Weekend (from Sep 2026)Light green cell backgroundYes – downtime for P systems; offline change for T/DYes
Optional / Unplanned Maintenance Weekend (from Sep 2026)Light grey cell backgroundPotential – for urgent/unplanned activitiesYes (precautionary)
Software Patching – Corrections only (HFC)Green box colorYes – uses software patching downtime windowYes
Software Patching – Corrections + Continuous DeliveryBrown box colorYes – uses software patching downtime windowYes
Software Patching – HFC with Critical Fixes (xx+)Brown box colorYes – uses software patching downtime windowYes
HANA Database UpgradePurple box colorYes – uses software patching downtime windowYes
System Upgrade (Major Release)Red box colorYes – uses system upgrade downtime windowYes
Backup Weekend for Previous UpgradeGrey box colorYes – for individual systems that missed prior upgradeYes (if applicable)

[1] [2] [3]

Key Clarifications on Downtime Duration

While every maintenance window type listed above is associated with a defined downtime window, SAP's official guidance makes two important qualifications: [2] [3] [4]

  1. Systems may be released earlier than the full contractual window if the maintenance activities do not require the complete downtime period. This applies to all types of maintenance activities. [2] [3]
  2. In practice, actual downtime is often shorter than the reserved window. For example, the reserved 4-hour weekly patching window typically amounts to approximately ½ to 1 hour on average — if used at all. Similarly, major upgrade actual end-user downtime averages closer to 2 hours, despite an 8-hour reserved window. [4]

However, these are averages and not guarantees. SAP does not commit to a shorter actual downtime in the SLA.

Contractual Maintenance Windows for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

For reference, the SLA-defined windows are: [5]

Region Weekly Maintenance Window Major Upgrade Window
MENAFRI 7 pm (4 hrs)SAT 12 am (4 hrs)
APJSAT 3 pm (4 hrs)SAT 12 pm (4 hrs)
EuropeSAT 10 pm (4 hrs)SAT 7 pm (4 hrs)
AmericasSUN 4 am (4 hrs)SUN 1 am (4 hrs)
Recommendation
  • Treat all maintenance windows as potential downtime windows. The maintenance calendar does not designate any maintenance type as fully "non-disruptive" for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Every maintenance type shown in the calendar is associated with a downtime window. [2] [3]
  • Plan API suspension for the full contractual window, not just the expected average. Since systems "may be released earlier" but this is not guaranteed, integrations should be designed to handle the full reserved window gracefully (e.g., via retry logic, queuing, or scheduled suspension). [2] [3]
  • Subscribe to Cloud System Notification Subscriptions (CSNS) at https://me.sap.com/systemsprovisioning/getNotified to receive advance notifications of planned and unplanned downtimes for your specific systems. [6]
  • Monitor the SAP for Me / Cloud Availability Center (CAC) and Cloud ALM, where SAP publishes downtime window information for HFC deployments. [3]
  • For half-yearly upgrades, customers are notified approximately 6 weeks in advance via email, providing sufficient lead time to plan API suspension. [7]

Note: The specific maintenance calendar document you referenced (sap.com/documents/2021/09/...) is the authoritative source for exact dates. The color-coding legend described above is the key to interpreting whether a given weekend involves a software patch, infrastructure maintenance, upgrade, or backup activity — but all of them carry a downtime window. [1] [2] [3]

entry.title: Re: the Node Reference doesn‘t work in DMEE Format
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Here is the question our internal chatbot provides. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,
Henrike

#AI-Generated Content

DMEE: Why Node Reference to Aggregation Node Fails — and How to Solve It

Root Cause: DMEE Processing Sequence

This is a fundamental processing-order constraint in DMEE. The engine processes the format tree top-down and left-to-right in a single pass. The critical issue is:
  • Your SUM (Aggregation) technical node accumulates values incrementally as it iterates over payment items (line by line).
  • At the moment DMEE evaluates the condition on FPSFlg, the loop has not yet completed — the SUM node's final accumulated value is therefore not yet available (it is still zero or incomplete at that point in the processing pass).
  • A Node Reference in a condition resolves the current value of the referenced node at the instant the condition is checked — for an aggregation node still mid-loop, that value is meaningless.
This is why the Node Reference to SUM appears to do nothing or always returns 0.

The Three Valid Solutions

Solution 1 — Reference the Source Field Directly (Recommended)

This is the cleanest approach. The SAP payment program (F110 / SAPF110V) already computes the total payment amount at run time. It is available in the payment medium data structure before DMEE starts its tree traversal.
 
Scenario Field to Reference
Classic payment programREGUH-ZBTR (total house-bank amount)
Payment Medium WorkbenchThe corresponding amount field at the payment header level in your data selection
Steps in the FPSFlg condition:
  1. Open the node FPSFlg → go to the Condition tab.
  2. Set the Left-Hand Side type to Source Field (not "Node Reference").
  3. Enter the data structure/field (e.g., REGUH-ZBTR).
  4. Set the operator to < and the Right-Hand Side constant to 200000.
This bypasses the aggregation node entirely, because the source data already has the answer.

Solution 2 — Restructure the Tree Using a Pre-Aggregation Level

If you genuinely need to aggregate in DMEE (e.g., summing across multiple line items into a group total), the aggregation node must complete its loop before the node consuming its result is evaluated. This requires restructuring:
[Header Loop / Company Code Level]
   └── [SUM]  ← Aggregation node lives HERE, at the PARENT level
               ← It completes before children of this level are processed
   └── [FPSFlg]  ← Now evaluated AFTER SUM is finalized for this header
       └── [Condition: Node Reference → SUM < 200000]
The rule is: the referenced aggregation node must be a preceding sibling (or at a parent level) that closes its loop before FPSFlg is reached. If SUM and FPSFlg are inside the same repeating loop, the reference will always see an incomplete value.

Solution 3 — Use a Formula with ABAP User Exit (DMEEX)

In the Extended DMEE (DMEEX), node conditions support Formulas that can call custom function modules. You can write a short function module that:
  1. Reads the payment total from REGUH for the current payment run.
  2. Returns a flag ('X' or ' ') based on the threshold.
Then in FPSFlg's Value tab or Condition tab, reference the formula result. This gives full flexibility but requires an ABAP enhancement.
Note for S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: In-app extensibility is restricted. You can use Key User Extensibility tools, but classical ABAP user exits in DMEE are typically not available in the Public Cloud edition. Solution 1 (direct source field reference) is therefore the most practical path for your environment.

Summary

 
Approach Works in S/4HANA Cloud PE? Complexity
Source Field Reference (REGUH-ZBTR)YesLow
Tree restructure (aggregation at parent level)YesMedium
ABAP User Exit / FormulaNot in Public EditionHigh
The reason your Node Reference to SUM does not work is not a configuration mistake — it is a documented behavioral constraint: aggregation values are only finalized after their iteration completes, but node reference conditions are evaluated during (not after) the same iteration. Pointing directly to the source data field is both simpler and more reliable.
Useful SAP Help Portal references:
  • Reference Conditions (DMEE)
  • Extended Data Medium Exchange Engine (DMEEX)

Cloud Print Manager: Multiple Paper Tray Handling in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
Recommended Approach
  • The best practice for handling multiple paper trays on a single physical printer is to create one dedicated print queue per tray in the Maintain Print Queues app. Each print queue acts as a virtual connection between the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system and a specific tray configuration on the local printer. [1]
  • You must create custom print queues (not the DEFAULT queue, which cannot be used for productive output and cannot be linked to the SAP Cloud Print Manager for Pull Integration). [2] [3]
  • Each print queue is then configured in the SAP Cloud Print Manager for Pull Integration (SAP CPM for PI), where the queue is mapped to the physical printer and its specific tray settings. [4] [5]
Tray Assignment in Cloud Print Manager

How tray selection works via PDF Settings:

  • In the SAP Cloud Print Manager for Pull Integration, each print queue has a PDF Settings configuration (available only for queues with PDF format). Within PDF Settings, the following options are relevant to tray handling: [6] [7]
    • Fit paper size: Scales the print settings in accordance with the paper size in the paper tray while preserving the aspect ratio of the original document.
    • Ignore paper size: Prevents the printer from requesting manual confirmation when a document with an invalid paper size is sent to a tray (e.g., a Letter document sent to an A4 tray).
    • Ignore print profile: When this option is deselected, CPM sends printer-specific properties (including tray selection, duplex mode, color mode, etc.) from the attached printer to the print queue in the SAP Cloud system. These properties can then be used to define print profiles for a print queue item. [6] [7] [8]

Whether tray detection is automatic or requires manual configuration:

  • Tray selection is not automatically detected from the printer. The SAP CPM for PI sends printer-specific properties to the cloud system when "Ignore print profile" is not selected — but the actual tray assignment requires deliberate configuration. [6] [8]
  • To use queue-specific print settings (including tray selection), you must:
    1. In CPM for PI PDF Settings, remove (deselect) the "Ignore print profile" option for the relevant print queue.
    2. In the SAP S/4HANA Cloud app Maintain Print Queues, select the relevant print queue and click "Manage Print Profiles" to configure queue-specific print settings, including tray selection. [8]
  • Note: Print profiles are not loaded when printing is triggered via the "Create Test Page" button in the print queue. You must trigger printing from the business application to test print profiles. [8]

For IFbA (Interactive Forms by Adobe / Adobe Forms) specifically:

  • Tray control when printing IFbA forms via CPM has a dedicated configuration path. SAP KBA 2682496 covers this scenario specifically, including the use of the ISR tray selection option in PDF Settings — however, this option is explicitly noted as being for Swiss payment form printing only and should not be used for other printing scenarios. [6] [9]
  • For Adobe Forms more broadly, tray control options include Job Profiles (SAP Notes 1743567, 2111085) and XDC file configuration, though these are more relevant to on-premise/private cloud spool-based environments. [10] [11]
Output Determination Integration
  • Output Parameter Determination (via the Output Parameter Determination app, using BRF+/BRFs business rules) is the mechanism that routes print jobs to specific print queues. [1] [2] [12]
  • In the Printer Settings determination step, the field Print Queue defines which queue a document is routed to. This can be conditioned on attributes such as:
    • Purchasing Organization
    • Document Type
    • Supplier Number
    • Company Code, and other application-specific fields [2]
  • By creating one print queue per tray and configuring Output Parameter Determination rules accordingly, you can automate routing of specific document types (e.g., invoices to tray 1, delivery notes to tray 2) to the correct queue — and therefore to the correct tray. [1] [2]
  • This is the standard best practice: Output Parameter Determination handles the routing logic (which queue), and CPM for PI + Print Profiles handle the physical tray assignment (which tray on the printer). [12] [8]
Key Considerations
  • Multiple queue options: SAP supports several configurations for assigning print users to print queues and connecting them to printers via CPM for PI — including multiple queues to one CPM server, or separate CPM servers per queue. Choose the topology that fits your infrastructure. [2]
  • Print profile activation: Queue-specific tray settings only take effect when "Ignore print profile" is deselected in CPM PDF Settings AND print profiles are maintained in the Maintain Print Queues app. If "Ignore print profile" is active, only the global CPM default settings are used. [8]
  • PDF format requirement: The PDF Settings (including tray-related options) are only available for print queues configured with PDF format. [6] [7]
  • SAP Note 2757763 covers how to print to multiple print queues or generate multiple output items — this is a useful reference for multi-queue scenarios. [2]
  • Testing: Always test print profiles by triggering output from the business application, not from the "Create Test Page" button in the print queue, as print profiles are not loaded during test page printing. [8]
  • SAP_COM_0466: The communication arrangement based on this scenario is required for CPM for PI to authenticate and poll print queues. Retrieve the System URL from this communication arrangement. [2] [13]

entry.title: Making AI Real: Black Horse One Galloping Towards New AI Opportunities
entry.content:
Here’s another nice example of Making AI Real with SAP Business AI Platform.

The reality is that many organizations aren’t yet ready to get the full benefits of artificial intelligence. In order to take a big leap forward, they have to take a small step back and make sure they have a solid platform in place.

That’s a good summary of my conversation with Daniel Göhlen, the founder of Black Horse One, a company specialized in equestrian innovation. The organization has a very atypical profile for a SAP customer: just 12 people, eight of whom are full time, and they do not use SAP ERP, only functionalities that are now part of the SAP Business AI platform, including integration and data analysis.

The company was founded as a startup, with the mission to support equestrian sports such as dressage — which the Fédération Équestre Internationale (FEI) describes as the “ultimate expression of horse training and elegance,” a complex sport where human and equine athletes compete at events all over the world, evaluated by judges and spectators in an array of categories that prize beauty, grace, and tradition.

Using SAP technology they have been able to get rid of manual, paper-based processes such as the judges’ scoring, and — more importantly — make the sport more interesting and engaging for fans. Dressage has been described as like judging ice skating competitions, but with riders and their horses. There’s the same notion of a set of figures that have to be completed, with scoring individual parts of the routine for difficulty and overall artistry.

Black Horse One started their journey by providing a small group of officials with iPads and an application that allowed them to score the competitions more easily. But now they cover many different aspects of the sport, with two to three million people now using the software on a regular basis. The ability to update, calculate, and share information in real time, during the competitions, was a key element in the organization’s choice of the SAP platform.

Their challenges have been ones that will be familiar to anybody reading this — such as unified and harmonized data. In their case, that means being able to use elements of the platform such as SAP Business Data Cloud to track if a horse moves from one federation to another, even though that means they end up with a different identifier. For example, the owners may live in a border region, competing in both Germany and the Netherlands, with different IDs. Being able to track the full horse history is important, especially for things like tracking horse welfare — the equestrian equivalent of predictive maintenance, making sure that the “equipment” is getting all of the care it deserves.

So where does AI come in? Daniel notes that Black Horse One is still in the early stages of exploring the “tremendous” potential of AI, but because his organization has one of the largest data set within the equestrian sphere, there are some big opportunities. For example training is obviously a key focus, and so they have created an application that tracks and extracts everything that trainers need track performance.

And Black Horse One is using AI to make a direct difference to the fan experience. For example, at smaller venues, there often isn’t a dedicated, knowledgeable announcer for the event. The organization offers organizers the possibility of AI announcers, complete with the voices of well-known stars of the industry, who give real-time results and statistics from the platform in order to keep the crowds engaged and help recreate the bigger-venue feel.

Daniel finished up our session with a message for other small organizations that might hesitate to use a product like SAP: “Even if you are such a small company, give it a shot. I can really recommend it ... for our mission critical processes, SAP is the way to go and we'll definitely stick with it."

To learn more about how Black Horse One brought digital transformation to the tradition-bound world of equestrian sports, check out the links below, and see the full series of SAP Customer Conversations: Better Together episodes for more best practices and lessons learned.

  • My official SAP News article
  • Thought leadership podcast: Göhlen, CEO of Black Horse One, talks with Tamara McCleary, CEO of Thulium, to share his motivation and journey merging tradition with technology to transform equestrian events, improving the sport and the sporting experience for athletes and audiences and winning over even the most traditional participants.
  • Practitioners’ video: Göhlen talks with me about what it took and the technologies that have resulted in a suite of applications that revolutionized the dressage world.

entry.title: From incident to insight: How SAP RootMap transforms RCA creation
entry.content:
The process to figure out what went wrong is called a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and is critical to both keeping customers informed and to creating lessons learned reports so SAP can work to prevent the next failure. The manual process is time-consuming. Investigators must manually pull together records, notes, and timelines from multiple sources, a process that takes an average of 15 hours per incident when accounting for cross-team coordination, research, validation, and final findings approval.

SAP RootMap cuts that time to under two minutes for the initial RCA draft. The tool automatically retrieves incident records from SAP's internal systems and uses AI to produce a structured report. Instead of spending hours collecting data, problem managers start with a ready-made summary and spend their time reviewing, refining, and approving the findings.

RootMap retrieves key incident details automatically, including the issue's priority, affected region(s), impacted Lines of Business, assignment groups, work notes, bridge call notes, and structured timeline entries. These entries help reconstruct critical milestones such as when experts were engaged, when infrastructure was restored, and when customers were notified. Where linked issue records exist, RootMap also incorporates documented cause notes and prior RCA material. Managers review the draft for any missing or unconfirmed details before it is finalized.

The real-world impact is clear. When a major downtime hits a hyperscaler's region on 9 October 2026, RootMap assembled the full picture in minutes, covering numerous timeline entries, bridge call notes, cause notes, and restoration timestamps. The incident, which impacted 1,132 productive customer tenants across six SAP product lines (including S/4HANA, SuccessFactors, BTP, HANA Cloud, and more) lasted approximately 14 hours and 30 minutes. Work that would have taken the team hours to organize manually was ready for review almost immediately.

From a single incident, a problem manager can produce three versions of the same report, each shaped for a different audience. Engineers receive a detailed technical breakdown of the failure. Executives receive a short, plain-language summary. And governance and review teams receive a clear event timeline that highlights system availability gaps. Additionally, a built-in chatbot handles adjustments, accepting plain language requests from managers such as “simplify this for leadership.” The tool then updates the content on the spot before final report exports to Microsoft Word or to PowerPoint.

With hundreds of RCAs completed each year, the cumulative time savings for the Cloud Service Management team are significant. Generating an initial draft now takes under two minutes, compared to the hours that that step previously required. The process frees up hundreds of engineering hours annually, time that can go toward preventing the next Major Incident rather than documenting the last one.

Experienced problem managers still run each investigation and own the process from start to finish. They validate every finding, fill in any gaps, and approve the final report. The AI handles the data gathering and initial drafting so that the problem managers can focus on the analysis and judgment that the work demands.

SAP RootMap soft-launched on 25 June 2026 for CSM’s Quality & Reliability Management Problem Management team. Future updates aim to deliver a draft RCA within an hour of incident resolution, automating even more of the post-incident workflow. A resolved incident is the starting point for learning how to better prevent recurrence and rebuild customer trust. SAP RootMap makes that process faster, clearer, and more consistent.
